note.explanation: Solubility tells us how much solute can dissolve in a fixed amount of solvent at a particular temperature. Heating often increases the solubility of solids, but not always; the effect depends on the substance. Cooling a hot, concentrated solution can make crystals form.
examples: KNO₃ becomes much more soluble in hot water, so it can crystallize when the solution cools.
Gas solubility usually decreases as temperature rises, so cold soda water keeps more carbon dioxide dissolved.
note.checkAnswer: Most solids become more soluble when heated, but some solids and gases do not.
note.simple: Heating often helps more solid dissolve, while cooling can make some dissolved solid form crystals. This is not true for every substance.
note.checkQuestion: What usually happens to the solubility of a gas in water when the temperature increases?
note.title: How temperature affects solubility
steps: Compare how much solute dissolves at different temperatures.
For many solids, heating increases the amount that dissolves.
Cooling such a solution may cause some dissolved solute to form crystals.
Remember that some solids show little change or become less soluble when heated; gases usually become less soluble.
note.answer: Temperature usually increases the solubility of solids, but the effect varies by substance; gas solubility usually decreases as temperature increases.

written.text: Q1.1. Preparation of solutions leads to an important process in chemistry which enables us to purify a compound through crystallization. Describe a process in which potassium nitrate is purified by crystallizing it in water.
written.finalAnswer: Dissolve impure potassium nitrate in a small amount of hot water, filter off insoluble impurities, cool the solution so potassium nitrate crystals form, then filter, wash with a little cold water and dry the crystals.

explain.title: What solubility means
explain.body: The solubility of a solute is the amount of solute which can dissolve in 100g of a solvent at a particular temperature. Always include the 100 g of solvent and the temperature in a definition answer.

explain.title: Temperature usually increases solid solubility
explain.body: Many solids, including potassium nitrate, silver nitrate and potassium chloride, become more soluble in water as temperature increases. The sugar activity demonstrates this trend.

explain.title: The trend has exceptions
explain.body: Temperature does not affect every substance in the same way. Sodium chloride's solubility does not increase appreciably; lithium carbonate, calcium chromate and calcium hydroxide become less soluble as temperature rises.

explain.title: Gases and useful applications
explain.body: The solubility of gases in water generally decreases when temperature rises. Cooling soda water helps keep carbon dioxide dissolved. Temperature changes can also help purify solids by crystallization.

mistakes: Defining solubility without stating that it is measured in 100 g of solvent at a particular temperature.
Writing that solubility always increases when temperature increases; the section gives exceptions.
Saying NaCl and KNO₃ behave alike when cooled; NaCl solubility changes little, while KNO₃ solubility changes considerably.
For crystallization, forgetting to cool the solution or to filter out insoluble impurities before cooling.
